## Design brief (initial constraints)

Outdoor site: crowds spread less evenly than indoors and service access matters, so aisles are wider and every gate keeps a deeper clearance. K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main, out of the walking line. Food trucks will draw queues; their placement is left to the solver and checked against the simulation before anything is moved. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it.

- min_aisle_width 3 → 3.5 m
- door_clearance 5 → 6 m
- K1 pinned at (18, 1) beside G-main

Booth coordinates were then computed by the layout solver under these constraints.

## What changed and why

No changes were applied to the baseline layout.

- Pedestrian metrics come from the engine's JuPedSim simulation; one scenario and seed per run, so results are a single sample, not a distribution.
- Booth popularity values are planning estimates of relative attraction, taken as given.
- Densities are peak values per grid cell over the run; hotspot thresholds are the engine's. Travel times count finished agents only.
- Geometric checks cover booth/obstacle/door-clearance/aisle rules only; egress capacity, fire code and accessibility were not assessed.

K1 sells tickets, so it sits beside G-main, out of the walking line. Food trucks will draw queues; their placement is left to the solver and checked against the simulation before anything is moved. The fire lane is unbuildable and must stay continuous; the engine enforces it. The solver placed the booths of Riverside Park Plaza (60m x 40m, outdoor) under those constraints and the layout was simulated under one fixed scenario. The worst congestion is hotspot #0. High-attraction booth M04 draws visitors into this zone.

Across 1 revision it kept the layout as stable as possible and changed only what the simulation pointed at: High-attraction booth M04 sits in the entrance inflow; requiring popular booths to keep a distance from entrances separates arriving visitors from booth crowds. This releases the requested positions of F1, F2, F3, F5 (pinned by the input constraints), so it needs the organizer's approval. Each revised layout was re-validated and re-simulated with the identical scenario, so the before/after comparison below reflects layout changes only.
